hook.line: Salsa on Friday, football on Sunday, a party in Medellín, and only one Tomás. He's stuck, and Spanish has the exact words for being stuck.
hook.en: I don't know what to do.

examples.en: I don't know what to do.
I don't know whether to go.

examples.es: No sé dónde dejar el carro.
examples.en: I don't know where to leave the car.

examples.es: No sé qué ponerme para la fiesta.
examples.en: I don't know what to wear to the party.
I didn't know how to tell him.

examples.es: No sé si cancelar la cita.
examples.en: I don't know whether to cancel the date.

rule:
This one copies English nicely: I don't know what to do is *no sé qué hacer*.
*No sé* plus a question word plus the dictionary form of the verb.
*qué*: what to
*cómo*: how to
*dónde*: where to
*a quién*: who to
*si*: whether to

The question words keep their accents: *qué*, *cómo*, *dónde*. Only *si* (whether) has none.

English needs to before the verb. Spanish doesn't: *hacer* already means to do.

It works with other people and the past too: *Vale no sabe qué ponerse*, *no sabía qué decir*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this an indirect question with an infinitive. It only works when the person who doesn't know is the one who'd do it.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *qué* or *que* and type the whole sentence: No sé ___ hacer. (I don't know what to do.)
yourTurn.why: What to is a question word, so it keeps its accent: *qué*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *si* or *sí* and type the whole sentence: No sé ___ ir. (I don't know whether to go.)
Say: I don't know where to leave the car.
yourTurn.answer: No sé dónde dejar el carro.
yourTurn.why: Where to is *dónde* plus the dictionary form: *dejar*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I don't know whether to cancel the date.
yourTurn.answer: No sé si cancelar la cita.
yourTurn.why: Whether to is *si* plus the dictionary form, no extra word for to.

yourTurn.prompt: Put it in the past: *No sé qué decir.* (I didn't know what to say.)
yourTurn.why: Only *sé* changes, to *sabía*; the rest stays the same.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about Tomás: *No sé qué hacer.*

pitfalls.why: Close. Here *qué* means what, so it needs its accent.
Close. English needs to, but Spanish doesn't: *hacer* already means to do, so no *para*.
Whether is *si* with no accent. *Sí* means yes.

personal: Think of a small decision you're stuck on right now and say it: *No sé si...* or *No sé qué...*
